॥ Om, by the distinction of attributes and by the denial of difference, neither of these two is [the ultimate reality]. ॥ 1/2/22 ॥

From the attributes in the statement, “He who is omniscient, all-knowing, whose austerity is made of knowledge,” Nature (Prakriti) is not [the ultimate reality]. From the denial of difference in the statement, “Therefore, from this Brahman, name, form, and food are born,” Virinca is not [the ultimate reality]. From the tripartite designation in the Skanda Purana, “The other, the Imperishable, that is Nature, of inert form; the Supreme Nature is declared to be Consciousness, dependent on Vishnu. They call that Imperishable the Supreme, and beyond the Supreme, the Supreme Imperishable. Hari alone is considered to be the triad of Imperishables, possessing all qualities,” the phrase “beyond the Imperishable, the Supreme” is also merely an attribute. From the denial of difference in the statement, “When he sees another, the Lord, and beholds His majesty, he is free from sorrow,” even the one who has attained the status of Ishana is not Rudra. ॥ 22 ॥
